definitions: A cast-iron or forged-steel fluke assembly of considerable heft, lowered to bite into the seabed and hold a vessel fast against wind, current, and second thoughts.
colloq. The one object on a ship guaranteed to win a staring contest with gravity.
example: The anchor came down with a clang that rattled every coffee cup in the galley.
etymology: From Old English ancor, by way of Latin ancora and Greek ankyra. Three languages, one unbothered slab of metal.
caption: Plate CXXXII., A venerable ship's anchor, resting on the dock with the unhurried confidence of an object nobody has ever asked to move by hand.
